invariant: Never accept a terminal/exit status alone as evidence a dispatched task, check, or run succeeded; verify the declared deliverable artifact.
procedural_substitute: Before marking any dispatched task, job, or gate complete, verify the declared deliverable artifact directly (file exists with expected content or row count, PR present, live round-trip fetch) rather than trusting exit code, HTTP 200, a 'done' label, or a bridge exit message alone; re-verify liveness by artifact growth/stability, not by process or harness exit signals.

invariant: A sandboxed task that needs network access or writes outside the sandbox default must have that capability explicitly granted and probed before it is relied on.
procedural_substitute: When a task needs network access or write access outside the sandbox default, grant it explicitly in the sandbox config (network_access, writable_roots) and run a post-deploy in-sandbox health probe that exercises the granted capability end-to-end before depending on it in the real task.

invariant: A task's delivery/routing decision must read one explicit, producer-set signal, never be inferred from report shape or a side-channel label.
procedural_substitute: Route a task's delivery/disposition off one explicit, producer-set field (e.g. expected_delivery) recorded at enqueue time; never infer delivery mode from report prose shape or a side-channel label the producing path did not itself set.

invariant: A dispatch capability must be validated against a known registry at enqueue time, bound to exactly one intended consumer, and its credential identity verified by fingerprint after any provisioning change.
procedural_substitute: Validate a dispatch capability against a known-capability registry at enqueue time (reject unknowns with a structured error, e.g. HTTP 422); assign each capability exactly one intended consumer; verify token/credential identity by fingerprint against the secrets source after any provisioning change, confirmed by a canary claim against a known non-empty queue.

invariant: N-lane or N-reviewer agreement is not independent corroboration unless each lane used an independent prompt, objective, and vendor identity.
procedural_substitute: Before crediting N-lane or N-reviewer agreement as independent corroboration, confirm each lane used an independent prompt/objective and a distinct vendor/harness identity that fails closed rather than borrowing an ambient credential; reviewers that share a vendor, model, or cite the same secondary artifact count as N=1, not N.

invariant: A process check must never match on a pattern the checking command's own invocation can itself satisfy.
procedural_substitute: Match a process for kill or liveness check by PID, or by a token guaranteed absent from the checking command's own invocation, never by a substring/pattern (pkill -f, grep, pgrep -f) that can match the checker's own command line; corroborate a negative liveness result with a second signal (e.g. log growth) before acting on it.

invariant: A gate must assert on structured status and its own tested artifact locator, and a regression test for a live failure must be proven against the real system before it is encoded.
procedural_substitute: A gate must assert on structured status (not exit code alone) and report the concrete artifact locator it actually tested, so a mismatch is checkable; before writing a regression test for a live failure, reproduce that failure directly against the real system and record the confirmed exit code/error/log line before encoding it as the test.

invariant: In a shared or concurrently-used git checkout, the actual branch/ref and remote state must be verified immediately before any commit, push, reset, or worktree removal -- never assumed from a brief or a prior report.
procedural_substitute: In any shared or concurrently-used git checkout, verify the actual branch/ref (git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD / git branch --show-current) and remote state (fetch + ls-tree/log against origin) immediately before any commit, push, reset, or worktree-remove; never assume the target branch, base, or worktree ownership from a brief, a flag, or a prior agent's self-report.

invariant: Denying a capability by scrubbing one environment variable is incomplete unless every other reachable channel is enumerated and confirmed closed.
procedural_substitute: When denying a capability by scrubbing an environment variable, enumerate every reachable channel that could still carry it (same-user IPC: D-Bus session bus, keyring/agent sockets, shared memory) and verify each is actually closed; to test whether a channel causes a capability, remove it and confirm the removal took effect, then retest -- never substitute a flag or alternate config believed to bypass it.

invariant: A coordinator must never yield on a dispatched or background delegate without either a verified deliverable artifact or a confirmed-live process it is actively polling.
procedural_substitute: A coordinator must not yield on a dispatched or background delegate without either (1) a terminal receipt confirming the declared deliverable artifact exists (non-empty, matching the brief's subject), or (2) a verified-live background process/job-registry entry it is actively polling; never accept a self-reported 'waiting' or future-tense status as evidence of progress.

invariant: Merge-readiness must be gated on a check-run re-confirmed against the PR's current base, never a cached rollup or a check-run timestamp predating a rebase.
procedural_substitute: Gate merge-readiness on a check-run re-confirmed against the PR's current base commit (fetch + compare timestamps against the last CI-infra change on main), not a cached statusCheckRollup or a check-run timestamp predating a rebase or retarget; re-run any check invalidated by a base change before merging.

invariant: A git worktree removal is not safe merely because git permits it; untracked files, stash scope, and reflog/gc timing must all be checked first.
procedural_substitute: Before deleting a git worktree, audit it for untracked files (git status --porcelain) since git's removal safety guarantees cover tracked content only, and never assume a worktree's stash entries are scoped to that worktree (stash is per-repository); never run `git gc --prune=now` or `git reflog expire --all` in the same pass as a deletion whose reversibility is being claimed.
